title: The Essential Inman Park Dining Guide: 12 Restaurants to Try in Atlanta - NewsBreak
text:
By Andrea Janise ,
1 days ago Inman Park has no shortage of good places to eat. With the Eastside BeltLine Trail running through the neighborhood and Krog Street Market just steps away, it’s the kind of place where a quick walk can easily turn into drinks, dinner, and a few hours spent exploring. The dining scene is just as varied, mixing longtime neighborhood institutions with newer arrivals, romantic date-night destinations, lively patios, and casual spots perfect for a post-BeltLine bite.
From handmade pasta and wood-fired pizza to Persian cuisine, sushi, steaks, and cocktails, these are the Inman Park restaurants to put on your radar.
Mushi Ni Chefs Michael Le and Tanya Jimenez first built a following through pop-ups and their food stall at Chattahoochee Food Works before landing a permanent home for Mushi Ni in Inman Park in early 2026. The intimate dining room has a laid-back energy, with ’90s hip-hop providing the soundtrack and a menu that keeps things creative without taking itself too seriously. Start with a calamansi margarita and chicken yakitori, then add a few of the rotating bao buns to the table. The menu changes regularly, which is part of the fun, but expect an affordable, inventive meal that feels distinct from anything else in the neighborhood. 337 Elizabeth St. NE, Atlanta, mushini.com
BoccaLupo A longtime Inman Park favorite, BoccaLupo is a neighborhood spot that consistently delivers, with handmade pasta at the heart of the menu. The Black Spaghetti with hot Calabrese sausage, rock shrimp, and scallions is a standout, while seasonal dishes might include Short Rib Tortelli in umami broth or Sweet Corn Risotto with spot prawns, charred Vidalia onions, and jalapeño pesto. It’s an easy choice for an impressive meal without too much fuss. Grab a cocktail, order a few pastas for the table, and settle in. 753 Edgewood Ave. NE, Atlanta, boccalupoatl.com
Delbar Persian-inspired spreads, house-baked bread, grilled meats, and vibrant mezze define the shareable menu at Delbar. | Photo by Delbar Delbar is the kind of Inman Park restaurant that’s easy to recommend, whether for out-of-town guests, a date night, or a leisurely dinner with friends. The Persian menu offers plenty for the table to share, from skewers cooked over an open flame to Omani shrimp, lamb and za’atar hummus, and salmon kebabs. When the weather cooperates, the lively sidewalk patio is one of the neighborhood’s most inviting places to settle in. Come hungry, order generously, and finish the meal with a Turkish coffee. 870 Inman Village Pkwy. NE, Ste. 1, Atlanta, delbaratl.com
Yuji Modern Japanese Right on the BeltLine’s busy Eastside Trail, Yuji is made for a night out. The crosswalk location puts you right in the middle of the action, with people walking and biking by and a great indoor-outdoor energy when the weather is nice. The fresh sushi, robata and cocktails make it worth the splurge. For date night, start with the Chef’s Sashimi Board and add the Tempura Platter for the table. 667 Auburn Ave. NE, Ste. 122, Atlanta, yujiatlanta.com
Fritti If you’ve walked through Inman Park on a nice afternoon, chances are you’ve seen Fritti’s patio packed with people, wine glasses in hand and pizzas coming out of the kitchen. Perched on the corner of North Highland and Elizabeth, Fritti is an Inman Park favorite that specializes in wood-fired Neapolitan-style pizza, with plenty of options beyond the classic Margherita. Try the Pizza Sorrentina with smoked mozzarella, cherry tomatoes, basil and Parmigiano, or the Robiola e Pesto with goat cheese, mozzarella, roasted tomatoes and pesto. Add a salad, grab some wine and settle in for a proper Inman Park afternoon. 309 North Highland Ave. NE, Atlanta, frittiatl.com
BeetleCat BeetleCat’s Maine-style lobster roll is finished with brown butter, adding a rich, nutty flavor to the classic combination of chilled lobster and mayo. | Photo by Beetlecat BeetleCat works just as well for happy hour or brunch as it does for a full dinner. Head downstairs to the cocktail den for a more laid-back vibe, or grab a table on the airy patio for some Highland Avenue people-watching. Start with the savory fry bread topped with honey butter and nori, then move on to the lobster roll, moqueca stew, or one of the fresh fish offerings. Whatever you order, save room for the coconut pie with Chantilly cream—it’s a standout way to end the meal. 299 North Highland Ave. NE, Atlanta, beetlecatatl.com
Sotto Sotto For a classic Inman Park dinner, Sotto Sotto is hard to beat. The neighborhood institution has been serving handmade Italian fare for more than two decades and, as the sister restaurant to Fritti, offers a more intimate setting that’s long made it a date-night favorite. Start with the Caprese or Smoked Burrata before moving on to handmade pastas like the Tortelli di Menta with ricotta and fresh mint or Pappardelle with duck ragù. Seafood and steaks round out the menu for those looking beyond pasta. 313 North Highland Ave. NE, Atlanta, sottosottoatl.com
Kitty Dare A spread of salad, pasta, wine, and cocktails at Kitty Dare. | Photo by Heidi Harris The Mediterranean-inspired menu at Kitty Dare pairs well with the thoughtfully curated wine list, while the intimate dining room and tucked-away patio make for a relaxed setting. Try the Citrus Salmon over pearl couscous with lemon-dill yogurt and charred lemon, or the Bucatini and Shrimp with garlicky breadcrumbs. The Lamb Burger with tzatziki and harissa aioli is another standout, while the Lamb Lasagna with creamy béchamel delivers on comfort. 1029 Edgewood Ave. NE, Atlanta, kittydare.com
Bread & Butterfly Chef Demetrius Brown has turned Bread & Butterfly into one of Inman Park’s essential daytime stops, whether for coffee and pastries, breakfast, or a leisurely brunch. The French-inspired menu weaves in flavors from across the African diaspora, giving familiar dishes a distinctive point of view. The crispy fried potatoes are a brunch must, while the salmon toast and French omelette are also worth ordering. There’s a thoughtful cocktail menu, too. Brown is now bringing his culinary perspective to Summerhill with his new restaurant, Heritage . 290 Elizabeth St. NE Ste. F, Atlanta, bread-and-butterfly.com
Barcelona Wine Bar Paella with a spread of tapas at Barcelona Wine Bar. | Photo by Barcelona Wine Bar Barcelona Wine Bar may be a chain, but after more than a decade in Inman Park, it has earned its place as a neighborhood staple. It’s an easy choice for a bottle of wine, a table full of tapas, and a long, leisurely dinner with friends or a date. The wine list is extensive, so don’t hesitate to ask the staff for a recommendation. For the table, try the Gambas al Ajillo, Pulpo Gallego, or Prawns a la Parrilla. 240 North Highland Ave. NE, Atlanta, barcelonawinebar.com/location/inmanpark
Ticonderoga Club If you know, you know—and if Ticonderoga Club is only on your radar for cocktails, don’t sleep on the food. The Krog Street Market favorite has earned its place as an Atlanta institution with a kitchen that brings just as much personality as the bar. Dishes like Poh’s Eggplant with jasmine rice, Thai basil, and mint and the Wok Vegetables showcase the menu’s creative side, while the Tavern Chicken and Reef Burger are longtime favorites. The cocktails remain a major draw, with a bar team and industry following that have helped make Ticonderoga Club a destination in its own right. 99 Krog St. NE Ste. W, Atlanta, ticonderogaclub.com
Kevin Rathbun Steak Kevin Rathbun Steak offers a more approachable take on the steakhouse experience with its Steak & Frites. | Photo by Kevin Rathbun Steak Save room for a splurge at Kevin Rathbun Steak, a tucked-away Inman Park destination from longtime Atlanta chef Kevin Rathbun. Start with Yaya’s Eggplant, Lobster Fritters, or Blue Crab Fingers before moving on to the main attraction: steaks like the Dry-Aged Porterhouse for Two or Cowboy Ribeye. There’s also an impressive Wagyu selection for those looking to go all out. For a celebratory dinner—or a decadent finish to an Inman Park food crawl—it’s a fitting final stop. 154 Krog St. NE Ste. 200, Atlanta, kevinrathbunsteak.com
